title: U.S. House · Nebraska's 1st District
area: Lincoln and southeast Nebraska, including Norfolk and Columbus

context.text: Incumbent Mike Flood (R) advanced from the Republican primary unopposed. Christopher Backemeyer defeated Eric Moyer 57.6% to 42.4% in the Democratic primary. The Cook Political Report rated Nebraska's 1st District R+6 based on presidential voting patterns.

priorities.text: Opposition to abortion, including working to ban abortion and expand prohibitions on taxpayer funding for it.
Border security, including completing a border wall and expanding funding for Customs and Border Protection and ICE.
Support for domestic energy production, including ethanol, coal and natural gas.
Opposition to federal COVID-19 mandates, including vaccine and mask mandates.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website said he would work to ban abortions and expand prohibitions on taxpayer subsidies for abortion.
positions.quote: I'll work to ban abortions and expand prohibitions on taxpayer subsidies for abortion. Our tax dollars should never be used to subsidize abortions.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website called for completing a border wall and expanding CBP and ICE funding, and opposed any pathway to citizenship for people in the country illegally.
positions.quote: We must complete President Trump's border wall, expand funding for Customs and Border Protection and ICE, and close loopholes in our immigration laws. I oppose amnesty and any pathway to citizenship for illegal immigrants.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website said he would oppose any attempt to infringe on the right to keep and bear arms.
positions.quote: I will oppose any attempt to infringe on Americans' fundamental liberties, including our freedoms of speech and religion and our sacred right to keep and bear arms.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website said he opposes the Green New Deal and carbon taxes and favors an all-of-the-above energy approach including coal and natural gas.
positions.quote: I oppose the Green New Deal, mileage taxes, carbon taxes, and any other radical effort to shackle our economy.

positions.summary: In an April 2025 interview, said tariffs can be an effective tool and expressed confidence in the administration's tariff approach.
positions.quote: Tariffs can be an effective tool for securing victories for America.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement, said he supports extending the Affordable Care Act subsidies but only with reforms, and that he voted against an extension without reforms.
positions.quote: I have said all along that I support an extension of the subsidies but not without reforms, including the elimination of waste, fraud, and abuse that both Democrats and Republicans have acknowledged exists.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Financial Services (Subcommittees on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Inclusion, and Housing and Insurance) in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Co-sponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed the House in September 2026 and is intended to prevent data-center energy costs from being passed on to consumers.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for families on housing, energy, groceries and child care, including ending tariffs and expanding the Child Tax Credit.
Congressional oversight of the executive branch, including investigations and hearings.
Ethics reform: banning stock trading by members of Congress, enacting term limits, and overturning Citizens United.

positions.summary: Supports rebalancing the tax code so billionaires and corporations pay a larger share.
positions.quote: Rebalance the tax code so that billionaires and corporations pay their fair share

positions.summary: Supports a public health-insurance option, lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 60, and extending ACA premium tax credits.
positions.quote: Enact a true public option to guarantee universal coverage and force insurance companies to compete by offering lower prices and better coverage

positions.summary: Supports protecting abortion access in Nebraska and nationwide.
positions.quote: Protect a woman's right to choose in Nebraska and nationwide

positions.summary: Calls for rolling back tariffs, saying they have raised costs for farmers and consumers.
positions.quote: Roll back tariffs that are hurting Nebraska's farmers and driving up costs for producers and consumers

positions.summary: Supports strong border security paired with a pathway to citizenship, and would cut what he calls excess ICE detention funding.
positions.quote: Claw back nearly $75 billion in excess funding from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and prohibit the use of any federal funds to detain children

positions.summary: His 2026 campaign website lists reasserting Congressional war powers to authorize military actions among his priorities.
positions.quote: Avoid forever wars by reasserting Congressional war powers to authorize military actions and prevent unilateral presidential war-making

candidates.name: Dan Hartong
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey, or questionnaire answers found (his iVoterGuide profile lists the questionnaire as unanswered); no public statements on guide issues found.

candidates.name: Nik Sandman

priorities.text: Overhauling the farm subsidy program so farmers are paid a fair market price for their products.
Extending Medicare to all Americans equitably.

positions.summary: Supports extending Medicare coverage to all Americans.
positions.quote: I favor extending medicare to all Americans in a way that preserves our freedom. That is, equally to all.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey. A campaign website (niksandman.com) exists with a priorities page (including Medicare for All) that was not mined for further statements; no news questionnaire or debate appearance found (the Sept. 23 debate listed only Flood and Backemeyer).
